headline: AI now helps build AI, and labs are fighting on price
summary: This week the labs pointed AI at themselves. OpenAI says its models found up to 14% chip gains on AMD's flagship GPU IP, its researchers' AI use keeps rising exponentially, and Perplexity is putting 10,000 GPUs toward an automated AI researcher. At the same time, near-frontier power got cheaper: GPT-6.2 Astra came within 0.3 points of Claude Fable 5.2 on one benchmark in a third of the time, and open models now carry about 30% of enterprise tokens. Google added Gemini 4 Neon after Carbon and Hydrogen, while Microsoft calls Copilot the OS for work and Perplexity calls its app a mini workOS. Agent spend is real money now, with T3 Code passing $10M in API spend in one day. Stop betting on one model and start measuring every agent task by what it costs and what it ships.

threads.title: AI that builds AI
threads.line: Labs now use their own models to improve chips, research and the next model. Expect the release clock to keep shortening.

threads.title: Close enough, for less
threads.line: Near-frontier models now come cheaper and from more vendors. Test each task and keep two providers in play.

threads.title: Who owns the workday
threads.line: Assistants are competing to become the screen your people work in. Choose on purpose before habits choose for you.

threads.title: Price every merged PR
threads.line: Agent spend is large and rising. Tie it to verified, shipped work and run agents' code in sandboxes.

threads.title: Nvidia without Jensen
threads.line: The main AI chip supplier lost its founder CEO while demand stays high. Treat compute supply as a strategic risk.
